einzeiler: How the daring Doolittle Raid on Tokyo changed World War II naval strategy forever.
kurzfassung: Following the attack on Pearl Harbor, Lieutenant Colonel James Doolittle led 16 B-25 bombers on a surprise airstrike against the Japanese mainland. Although the physical damage was minimal and all planes were lost, the mission successfully boosted American morale and unnerved Japanese leadership. The resulting fallout included brutal reprisals in China and a strategic pivot that culminated in the pivotal Battle of Midway.
stichpunkte: President Franklin D. Roosevelt ordered an attack on the Japanese mainland following Pearl Harbor to boost American morale.
Lieutenant Colonel James Doolittle planned the mission using B-25 bombers launched from the USS Hornet in the Pacific.
A Japanese patrol boat spotted the carrier early, forcing the 16 bombers to launch roughly 200 miles further out than planned.
The bombers successfully struck Tokyo and other cities, causing minor physical damage and killing around 87 people.
Low on fuel and without landing lights in China, one plane diverted to the Soviet Union while the other 15 crash-landed or bailed out.
Japan launched a massive retaliatory campaign in China, killing up to 250,000 civilians suspected of aiding the American airmen.
The raid shocked Japanese leadership and prompted Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto to move up plans for the Midway Islands, leading to a major turning point in the war.

clips.hook: Medals of peace returned as bombs
clips.text: Several explosives carried on the mission featured Japanese friendship awards attached to them as a symbolic rejection of past cooperation.
Despite multiple complications during the flight, the vast majority of the participating airmen managed to avoid capture or death.
A wartime documentary earned its title from the remarkably brief duration it took the aviators to drop their payloads.

clips.hook: Rapid response compared to past eras
clips.text: Modern military readiness stands in stark contrast to the lengthy preparation times required at the dawn of the Second World War.
Search and rescue animals deployed during the September 11 attacks are remembered fondly for their dedicated service.

beschreibung:
The Doolittle Raid, with 16 planes targeting six different Japanese cities, allowed the United States to rebound after its devastating losses at Pearl Harbor.
